external_entities.name: shopper
external_entities.description: A shopper who browses the storefront and places orders.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API

external_entities.name: card processor
external_entities.description: A third-party processor that settles payments and sends payment status callbacks.
external_entities.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

processes.name: storefront API
processes.description: A Node service running on Cloud Run that provides the storefront and captures orders.
processes.source_excerpt: the storefront API, a Node service running on Cloud Run
processes.notes: MFA has not been rolled out for shopper accounts.
processes.technology: Node service running on Cloud Run

processes.name: order service
processes.description: A Python worker that processes orders and reads and writes order data.
processes.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network
processes.notes: The database password comes from an environment variable on the worker.

data_stores.name: orders-db
data_stores.description: A PostgreSQL database containing orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four live in a PostgreSQL database (orders-db)

data_stores.name: receipt archive
data_stores.description: A Cloud Storage bucket containing receipts for completed orders.
data_stores.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.

data_flows.name: place orders
data_flows.description: A shopper browses the storefront and places orders through the storefront API.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Shoppers browse the storefront and place orders through the storefront API
data_flows.authentication: email and password with session cookie; MFA: none

data_flows.name: submit order
data_flows.description: The storefront API calls the order service when a shopper submits an order.
data_flows.source_excerpt: When a shopper submits an order the storefront API calls the order service over gRPC.
data_flows.notes: There is no authentication on the gRPC call; the order service accepts anything that can reach it.

data_flows.name: read and write
data_flows.description: The order service reads and writes orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four in the database.
data_flows.source_excerpt: the order service reads and writes with a single application account that has full read/write
data_flows.notes: The password for the application account comes from an environment variable on the worker.
data_flows.authentication: single application account with full read/write

data_flows.name: write receipt
data_flows.description: The order service writes a receipt for every completed order to the receipt archive.
data_flows.source_excerpt: Every completed order also gets a receipt written to a Cloud Storage bucket we call the receipt archive.
data_flows.notes: The receipt records which order was written and that the order service wrote it.
data_flows.authentication: the order service's own service account

data_flows.name: settlement webhook
data_flows.description: The card processor posts a webhook to tell the storefront API that an order is paid.
data_flows.source_excerpt: After they settle a payment they POST a webhook back to the storefront API to tell us the order is paid.
data_flows.notes: The source states: "I would have to check how that callback is authenticated."
data_flows.data_description: Payment settlement status for an order

trust_boundaries.name: internet
trust_boundaries.description: The internet-facing zone from which shoppers reach the storefront API.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: It is the only thing we expose to the internet.

trust_boundaries.name: core network
trust_boundaries.description: The core network containing the order service.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: The order service is a Python worker in our core network

trust_boundaries.name: card processor
trust_boundaries.description: The third-party zone containing the card processor.
trust_boundaries.source_excerpt: Our card processor is a third party.

assumptions.assumption: The orders database is confidential because it contains shopper addresses and card-last-four alongside orders.
assumptions.basis: The source states that orders-db contains orders, shopper addresses and card-last-four; personal and payment data are confidential.

assumptions.assumption: The receipt archive is confidential because it contains receipts for completed orders.
assumptions.basis: The source states that every completed order produces a receipt in the archive; receipts are payment-related business records.
